name: Strelets Reconnaissance-Fire Terminal
representative_system: Sozvezdie-M2 'Strelets' automated reconnaissance and fire-control terminal

cost.display: Not publicly disclosed — a soldier-portable terminal, not a major platform, so pricing is not broken out in open reporting

key_facts.label: Function
key_facts.value: Target designation and fire-mission request from squad level

key_facts.label: Effect
key_facts.value: Pushes call-for-fire authority down to small units

short_role: Soldier-portable terminal that lets a small unit designate a target and request fire directly, without routing through a higher headquarters first.
characteristics: Ruggedized handheld/portable terminal used by reconnaissance and infantry sub-units
Passes target coordinates and imagery toward supporting fires with minimal intermediate handling
Part of a wider push to equip small units with their own targeting and communications tools rather than relying solely on higher-echelon assets
employment_notes: Represents the squad-level end of the distributed kill chain described in force-structure reporting on this war: infantry and reconnaissance sub-units increasingly find, decide and call fire using their own organic tools rather than only consuming targeting products pushed down from higher headquarters.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional fire support ran up a chain from observer to headquarters to guns. Pushing a targeting and fire-request terminal down to squad level is a concrete example of the kill chain becoming distributed rather than concentrated at higher headquarters — a structural change in who gets to call for fire, not just a faster version of the old process.

connections.description: Operator training pipeline for squad-level fire-control terminal crews.
